 Respiratory Protection Regulatory Engagement Specialist 
 Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World 
 Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.
 As a Respiratory Protection Regulatory Engagement Specialist in 3M’s Personal Safety Division (PSD), you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world.
 You will collaborate with multidisciplinary colleagues around the world to advance respiratory protection standards, regulations, and occupational health and safety (OHS) practices across global markets. You will represent 3M in high-impact regulatory and standards-development activities, engaging with OHS professionals, industry stakeholders, and regulators as a technical thought leader. In this role, you will shape science-based approaches and provide technical leadership.
 Here, you will make an impact by:
 Facilitating the development of science-based performance and selection and use standards for respiratory protection equipment and occupational health and safety, while tracking progress and key milestones.
 Identifying opportunities to advance respirator related health and safety policies and regulations and developing strategies to implement science-based approaches.
 Helping to coach, mentor, develop, and coordinate PSD’s global team of application engineers and regulatory specialists engaged in respiratory protection standards development activities.
 Collaborating with professional associations, educational organizations, public health organizations, and relevant government entities.
 Representing 3M in standards development organizations and related technical committees.
 Collaborating with cross-functional teams to align on PSD’s highest-priority respirator related standards and regulations that support business growth.
 Leading respirator related research to support new technologies and existing products.
 Communicating emerging respiratory protection standards, regulatory, and policy developments to relevant stakeholders and translating their potential implications into actionable business guidance.
 Your Skills and Expertise 
 To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M is looking for candidates who must have the following qualifications:  
 Bachelor’s degree or higher (completed and verified prior to start)
 Five (5) years of experience with respiratory protection-related occupational health and safety regulations and performance standards in a private, public, government or military environment.
 Master’s degree in occupational health and safety, industrial hygiene, public policy, regulatory affairs, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
 Experience representing an organization with regulatory agencies, standards-development organizations, industry associations, policymakers, or government affairs stakeholders.
 Experience conducting or leading applied research in respiratory protection or personal protective equipment.
 Ability to translate complex technical, regulatory, or policy information into clear guidance for diverse audiences.
 Strong communication, influencing, stakeholder-management, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
 Ability to work effectively across cultures, geographies, and global teams.

About the Role 
 As Program Specialist, Social Studies – Elementary (K–6), you own the instructional design and quality of the courses in your subject. You decide how learning is designed and built, and whether the content meets the bar to go live. You report to the Director, Content & Curriculum – Elementary (K–6). 
 You work in a course team. The Product Manager owns the product vision, plan, scope and dates. You shape the instructional vision within that product vision. You lead the Content Producers who report to you, full-time and freelance: you coach them, set craft standards and review their work, while the Product Manager sets the team’s priorities. 
 This role suits an experienced educator with deep social studies expertise and a strong grasp of how students develop in the subject. You are curious about how technology can improve the classroom. As the trusted voice of the classroom, you turn curriculum goals and classroom realities into engaging, effective and scalable learning in Edwin. 
 This posting represents an existing vacancy. 
 Key Accountabilities 
 Instructional design (30%) 
 Shape the instructional vision, learning outcomes and instructional approaches within the Product Manager’s product vision, during discovery and development. Contribute the instructional requirements to the Product Requirements Document (PRD). 
 Analyze new curriculum for what is new or different, and complete curriculum correlations. 
 Own the scope and sequence and learning pathways in Course Builder. Validate them with the Product Manager against the plan, and with Classroom Success and the Content Producers. 
 Own the subject instructional design style guide within our standard content development workflow, keeping it aligned with the curriculum, sound pedagogy, subject integrity, and real classroom use. 
 Design formative and summative assessment into every course from the start, to the K–12 assessment standards set by the Assessment Lead. Content Producers build the items. 
 Lead the thoughtful use of digital tools and emerging technologies in learning design. 
 Content quality (25%) 
 Serve as the subject-matter expert and educational advisor across the elementary social studies portfolio. 
 Build and validate the first content prototype with Content Producers for early review. 
 Own the authoring instructions Content Producers use to create content, making sure they reflect the instructional design 
 Own quality throughout the build: accuracy, instructional integrity, CRRP alignment and classroom usability. Arbitrate review decisions; if the Product Manager disagrees, the Director breaks the tie. 
 Make sure all specialty content, such as First Nations, Métis and Inuit content, is created and reviewed by appropriate Indigenous voices. 
 Give quality sign-off before the Product Manager’s go-live decision. 
 Advise the Product Manager on accessibility, so the instructional design supports AODA (WCAG 2.2 AA). 
 Team leadership (25%) 
 Hire, supervise, coach and develop the Content Producers who report to you, and own their performance reviews, with formal input from the Product Managers they work with. 
 Onboard, train and direct Content Producers (full-time and freelance), authors and reviewers in pedagogy, the instructional design and classroom best practice. Give contributors clear feedback, and liaise with Content Services. 
 Define contributor skill sets, special skills (such as Indigenous perspectives and safety) and staffing needs with the Product Manager. 
 Voice of the classroom (10%) 
 Engage teachers, students and education stakeholders through classroom observations, user research, conferences and educator conversations, feeding the Product Manager’s discovery. Follow board research approval processes and Nelson’s privacy policies. 
 Build launch supports with the Product Manager, and train Commercial colleagues and customers after launch. 
 Support the Product Manager’s RFP and procurement responses, presentations and go-to-market initiatives. 
 Continuous improvement (10%) 
 Use performance data, educator feedback and student impact to optimize, update, reuse and scale high-performing content. 
 Carry out refreshes of existing content with Content Producers, including retrofitting assessment into existing courses, on the Product Manager’s plan. 
 Bring subject-specific feature requests to the Product Manager, and keep the Product Manager and Director updated on quality issues. 
 What Success Looks Like 
 Make sure the scope and sequence, style guide, and content creation guidelines are ready by the dates set in the course plan. 
 Content passes review with few defects, and few quality issues are found after launch. 
 Teacher feedback rates the instructional quality of your courses highly. 
 Content Producers grow in capability, and are engaged and retained. 
 Requirements 
 University degree; certified educator (OCT or equivalent) preferred 
 7+ years of K–12 classroom or education experience, ideally in social studies 
 5+ years of content development and lesson creation in K–12, EdTech or digital learning 
 Deep social studies expertise, including student developmental trajectories, curriculum and assessment, across Ontario, Alberta and other provincial curricula 
 Strong instructional design and assessment design skills, translating curriculum into engaging learning experiences 
 People management experience (Content Producers report to this role) 
 Comfortable working in content authoring tools and digital content workflows; HTML an asset 
 Familiarity with emerging educational technologies and their classroom applications 
 Strong communication, collaboration and mentoring skills 
 Highly organized, adaptable and comfortable in a fast-paced environment 
 Strong commitment to improving student outcomes and educator experiences 
 Quick to master new tools for building content and working; judges all content critically against curriculum and pedagogy 
 French an asset 
 Who You Are 
 You bring 7+ years as a teacher, instructional coach or curriculum consultant, with deep subject expertise and a clear sense of how students develop across grades. 
 You design assessment as well as instruction, and you have led or coached other educators. 
 “If the design is right at the start, everything downstream gets easier.” 
 You coach producers rather than rewriting their work, and you enjoy watching them grow in skill. 
 You design with classroom data and Product Manager input, not alone. 
 You judge every draft critically against curriculum and pedagogy before it moves forward. 
 Creative problem solver: you find new ways to solve real teaching and learning problems, within our internal authoring tool, time and budget 
 UDL and differentiation: you meet every learner where they are, with entry points, supports and extensions 
 Modern and adaptable: you master new tools and techniques for building content and working quickly, and look for better ways of working, with expert judgment always leading 
 Compensation 
 The base salary for this permanent full-time position starts at $90,000 per annum based on experience. Compensation is part of our broader Total Rewards package, which includes benefits and programs that support employee well-being and growth.

 Sunlife is looking for someone to join our climate team on a one-year contract to support the measurement, management, and reporting of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across our supply chain. This role will play an important part in advancing quantification and assessment of supply chain emissions and supporting the development of processes, methodologies, and reporting capabilities related to Scope 3 emissions.  This work is in support of climate-related expectations associated with OSFI B-15 Climate Risk Management.
 Our ideal candidate has strong analytical skills with an interest in carbon accounting and environmental data management. The successful candidate will collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders across the organization, external partners and vendors to collect data and manage our inventory on a third-party carbon accounting data management platform. The individual will focus primarily on supply chain emissions, particularly Category 1 (Purchased Goods and Services) and Category 2 (Capital Goods), while also supporting other Scope 3 emissions categories and broader climate performance initiatives as needed.  
 At Sunlife, our purpose is to help our clients achieve lifetime financial security and lead healthier lives. Our focus on sustainability helps us bring this purpose to life. Our Climate Performance team acts as a central resource across the business, managing the development and reporting of our enterprise-wide GHG emissions, monitoring performance against targets, and supporting our global climate strategy and resiliency initiatives. Supporting the team’s efforts is a network of sustainability partners from business groups and regions in which we operate.
 What will you do? 
 Work across the Climate Performance team to support the development of the organization's GHG inventory and climate-related reporting:
 Contribute to the measurement and ongoing management of Category 1 (Purchased Goods and Services) and Category 2 (Capital Goods) emissions, including data collection, analysis, methodology refinement, and ongoing inventory maintenance
 Support the exploration, development, and implementation of measurement approaches for incremental supply chain emissions sources
 Support climate-related emissions analysis associated with digital technology and compute 
 Contribute to climate-related reporting, including the Sustainability Report, OSFI B-15 Climate Risk Management Report, ratings and rankings, and other internal and external disclosures
 Support the development and maintenance of key performance indicators (KPIs), metrics, and reporting processes used to monitor progress against climate commitments and targets
 Support assurance and assurance preparedness processes for select GHG emissions categories
 Assist with the implementation of regulatory requirements, standards, and best practices related to GHG accounting and sustainability reporting
 Identify opportunities to improve data quality, process efficiency, and automation within emissions measurement and reporting activities
 What do you need to succeed ?
 Degree in sustainability, environmental science, engineering, business, economics, data analytics, or a related field. 
 Knowledge of greenhouse gas accounting principles and an interest in developing expertise in the Greenhouse Gas Protocol
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with an ability to work with large and complex datasets
 Excellent attention to detail and ability to maintain high standards of data quality
 Strong oral and written communication skills
 Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and data analysis tools
 Experience with carbon accounting platforms, supply chain analytics, or ESG-related initiatives is a plus
 What’s in it for you? 
 We’re proud to be recognized as a company with a 2026 Most Trusted Executive team by Great Place to  Work® Canada
 Access to short-term assignments or ‘Gigs’ across the organization, to help you develop new skills and connections.
 A collaborative and interactive team environment
 Charitable giving through our You Give, We Give program lets you give back to your community – and in many  cases, we’ll match your contributions.
 Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to  support your well-being.

Procurify is the agentic procurement platform that helps mid-market organizations get complete control over their spend. We’re trusted by hundreds of companies around the world, across industries like biotechnology, education, health care, manufacturing, and software, to manage over $100B in spend. We’re looking for a talented and team-driven Senior Accountant to join us on our journey.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Procurify is looking for an experienced, detail-oriented, and systems-minded person who is passionate about accounting and building a streamlined, accurate, and well-controlled finance function. This role is ideal for a CPA (or equivalent designation such as US CPA or ACCA), or someone close to earning their designation, who is ready to join our Finance team as a Senior Accountant and take full ownership of our own use of the Procurify platform. This role reports to the Accounting Manager.

You are a person with a knack for owning the end-to-end accounts payable cycle and leading key accounting activities—including month-end close, reconciliations, payroll, sales tax compliance, and audit support—and you’re motivated by giving the business accurate, timely numbers it can rely on to make decisions. You enjoy improving processes and using technology to work smarter.

Everyone at Procurify is a team player. A big part of this role involves building strong relationships with vendors and internal teams, and acting as our voice of the customer to Product and Engineering as Procurify’s own power user. We’re seeking entrepreneurial people who are willing to challenge the status quo and contribute to larger strategic objectives.

We’re an AI-native team, and this role uses AI every day. You’ll build AI-assisted workflows across accounts payable, reconciliations, and month-end close, and you’ll bring the judgment to check AI output before it reaches the books.

WHAT YOU’LL BE WORKING ON:

Accounts Payable Cycle Ownership

 - Own the end-to-end accounts payable cycle, from vendor onboarding and invoice intake through approval, coding, payment, and reconciliation, including review of vendor bills and expense reimbursements.

 - Manage scheduled payment runs (EFT, ACH, wire, and cheque) and the vendor master file, validating banking details, tax forms, and supporting documentation.

 - Reconcile the AP sub-ledger to the general ledger and vendor statements, own prepaid schedules and amortization, and prepare AP aging, accrual, and cash requirement reports.

 - Serve as the main contact for vendor and internal AP inquiries, and strengthen controls such as approval workflows, segregation of duties, and verification of vendor banking changes.

Procurify Platform Ownership (Customer Zero)

 - Run purchasing, approvals, vendor bills, and payments for our own business in Procurify, acting as Finance’s superuser for configuration, workflows, and user support.

 - Act as customer zero by testing new features, including AI and payments capabilities, and sharing structured feedback on bugs, workflow gaps, and feature ideas with Product and Engineering.

Month-End Close & Reconciliations

 - Meet AP deadlines on the month-end close checklist, including AP accruals and prepaid amortization, and prepare variance analyses and supporting schedules for management.

 - Reconcile accounts payable, accrued liabilities, prepaids, and credit cards each month, automating manual steps where possible and keeping close documentation compliant with internal controls.

Payroll, Tax & Audit

 - Prepare the end-to-end payroll process, including data entry, wage calculations, variable compensation, and deductions.

 - Year end reconciliation and reporting, including statutory requirements.

 - Payroll compliance requirements across US and Canada.

 - Prepare provincial and GST/HST tax returns and annual audit working papers, act as the auditors’ point of contact for AP and month-end close, and complete ad hoc analysis for management.

Training & Team Development

 - Lead training and onboarding in your area, building training materials and guiding junior team members.

 - Develop and keep current the process documentation and desk procedures for AP, prepaids, credit card reconciliations, payroll, sales tax, and the AP close, and cross-train with accounts receivable to provide backup.

Process & System Improvements

 - Streamline accounting workflows and improve data accuracy through automation and AI tools, and support the Accounting Manager in rolling out new procedures and features.

 - Build AI-assisted workflows for AP, reconciliations, and month-end close, with documented review steps so controls and audit trails stay intact.

KPIS

 - On-time close: AP close tasks completed by the deadlines on the month-end close calendar.

 - Payment accuracy: Vendor payments made on time, to the correct payee and amount, with no duplicate or unauthorized payments.

 - Reconciliations: AP, accrued liabilities, prepaids, and credit card accounts reconciled and reviewed within the close window, with open items cleared or explained.

 - Payroll and tax filings: Canadian and US payroll runs and remittances, sales tax returns, and year-end slips filed accurately and by statutory deadlines.

 - Audit results: No material audit adjustments or control findings in the areas you own.

 - Customer zero feedback: Regular, structured feedback to Product and Engineering on bugs, workflow gaps, and feature ideas from running Procurify for our own business.

WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - 4–5 years of relevant accounting experience, preferably in SaaS, with hands-on ownership of a full-cycle AP function and Canadian and US payroll.

 - CPA Canada designation or an equivalent such as US CPA or ACCA, or currently enrolled in the CPA Professional Education Program (PEP) and close to completing your designation, plus a bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

Votre principal enjeu 
L’équipe Gametech Innovation réunit des profils de développement qui aident les équipes de jeu de Gameloft à créer de meilleurs jeux, en concevant des outils et des systèmes sur les moteurs Unity et Unreal qui couvrent un large éventail de besoins de production. En tant que Développeur ou Développeuse Mid-Level au sein de l’équipe, vous gérez la livraison de fonctionnalités et contribuez à la stabilité technique de nos outils et systèmes, sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie de chaque solution.
 Votre quotidien 
 Concevoir et livrer des outils aux équipes de jeu, de l’étude des solutions existantes et du prototypage d’alternatives jusqu’à la mise en production
 Développer en C++ et C# dans Unreal et Unity, avec un code lisible que toute l’équipe peut reprendre
 Déboguer et profiler ces outils sur console, PC et mobile pour qu’ils restent fiables en production
 Maintenir et faire évoluer les pipelines CI/CD et de build de l’équipe afin que les nouvelles versions des outils parviennent en continu aux équipes de jeu
 Utiliser des assistants de code basés sur l’IA au quotidien, tester de nouvelles approches et technologies, et proposer les améliorations incrémentales qui méritent d’être industrialisées
 À quoi ressemblera le succès 
Pendant vos trois premiers mois, vous prenez en main la base de code de l’équipe et vous livrez des correctifs et des fonctionnalités sur les outils existants avec un accompagnement limité. Entre le quatrième et le sixième mois, vous portez de bout en bout une fonctionnalité ou un sous-système, du benchmark à la livraison aux équipes de jeu. A partir de là, vous proposez de votre propre initiative des améliorations des outils et des workflows, et les équipes de jeu vous identifient comme point de contact technique.
 Avec qui vous travaillerez 
Vous reportez à la ou au Gametech Innovation Manager et collaborez très étroitement avec les autres membres de l’équipe Gametech Innovation, répartis dans plusieurs studios dans le monde, dont Paris, Montréal et Bucarest. Au quotidien, vous échangez avec les équipes de programmation, d’art technique et de production des équipes de jeu de Gameloft, à l’international.
 Votre parcours de recrutement 
 Premier entretien : une conversation pour explorer l’adéquation du poste avec votre parcours et répondre à vos principales questions.
 Test : vous recevez une courte étude de cas à réaliser.
 Deuxième entretien : vous rencontrez des membres de l’équipe technique pour présenter votre test et échanger plus en détail sur votre démarche, votre raisonnement et vos méthodes.
 Entretien final : vous rencontrez la Hiring Manager pour discuter de votre expérience, de votre vision et de votre façon d’aborder les sujets de technologie du jeu à un niveau plus large.
 Où ce poste peut vous mener 
Ce poste peut constituer un tremplin vers un poste plus senior au sein de l’équipe Gametech Innovation, ou vers une spécialisation dans un domaine précis comme la technologie de moteur, de pipeline ou de plateforme. Des formations internes et un mentorat assuré par les profils seniors de l’équipe sont disponibles, et une mobilité interne entre équipes et studios est possible grâce au programme Talent Move de Gameloft.
 ***
 WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON 
The Gametech Innovation team is a specialized group of developers focused on empowering Gameloft’s game teams to create better games through innovative technological solutions. We focus on Unity and Unreal engines, developing tools and systems that span a wide range of game development needs.
As a Mid-Level Developer within the team, you will manage feature delivery and support the technical stability of our tools and systems, contributing to the full lifecycle of each solution.
 What it means on a daily basis 
 Own features or subsystems end-to-end, from benchmarking existing solutions and prototyping alternatives through to implementing and shipping the final tool to game teams
 Write maintainable, self-explanatory code in C++ and C# within Unreal and Unity engines
 Debug and profile tools and systems across engines and target platforms (console, PC, mobile) so they stay reliable in production
 Maintain and extend the team's CI/CD and build pipelines so new tool versions reach game teams continuously
 Use AI coding assistants in your daily workflow, experiment with new approaches and technologies, and propose the incremental improvements worth industrialising
 What success will look like 
 In your first three months, you will be at ease in the team's codebase and delivering fixes and features on existing tools with limited guidance. From there, you will own a feature or subsystem end-to-end, you will propose improvements to tools and workflows on your own initiative and become a technical point of contact for the game teams we support.
 Who you would be working with 
 You will be reporting to our Gametech Innovation Manager, and collaborate very closely with other Developers from the Gametech Innovation team across multiple studios worldwide, including Paris, Montreal, Bucharest, and others, offering opportunities to collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and perspectives. Day to day you will work with game programmers, technical artists and producers on Gameloft's game teams internationally.
 Your recruitment journey 
 First interview: A conversation to explore how the role aligns with your background and to address your main questions.
 Test: You will receive a short case study to complete.
 Second interview: You will meet members of our technical team to present your test and talk through your approach, reasoning, and methodologies in more depth.
 Final interview: You will meet a Hiring Manager to discuss your experience, vision, and how you approach game technology topics at a broader level.
 Where this role can take you 
 This role can be a stepping stone toward a more senior position within the Gametech Innovation team, or toward specialising in a particular area such as engine, pipeline or platform technology. Internal training and mentoring from the team's senior developers are available, and internal mobility across teams and studios is possible through Gameloft's Talent Move programme.

Tenstorrent is seeking a highly skilled and experienced Engineer to lead post-silicon power characterization and correlation activities for cutting-edge semiconductor products. In this role, you will be responsible for developing and executing detailed power measurement strategies on silicon, correlating results with pre-silicon models, and driving improvements across power architecture, design, and modeling methodologies. You will serve as a key technical leader, interfacing across design, architecture, validation, and systems teams to ensure silicon meets power and performance specifications under all operating conditions.
 This role is hybrid, based out of Toronto, ON or Austin, TX or Santa Clara, CA.
 Who you are 
 A Principal-level engineer with 8+ years in silicon power analysis and characterization, and a Master’s or PhD in EE, CE, or related field.
 Deep understanding of digital and mixed-signal power domains, including DVFS, leakage vs. dynamic power, and power gating.
 Highly proficient in lab-based power measurement using oscilloscopes, current probes, power analyzers, and SMUs, plus Python/Perl/MATLAB for automation and analytics.
 A strong debugger and collaborator, comfortable driving cross-functional investigations and clearly communicating technical findings.
 What we need 
 Own the post-silicon power measurement strategy end-to-end across operating modes, voltages, frequencies, and workloads.
 Build and maintain lab infrastructure, automated workflows, and data analysis pipelines for high-fidelity, repeatable power characterization.
 Correlate silicon power data to pre-silicon models (RTL, gate-level, sign-off), drive root-cause analysis, and refine power estimation methodologies with design and modeling teams.
 Characterize power across PVT corners and work with bring-up/validation teams to develop test content, debug power anomalies, and ensure products meet power and performance specs.
 What you will learn 
 How state-of-the-art SoCs behave in real silicon across diverse workloads, system configurations, and operating conditions.
 How to influence power architecture, RTL design, and modeling flows by feeding silicon insights directly back into early design phases.
 Best practices for building scalable, automated post-silicon power infrastructures that support multiple products and generations.
 Advanced correlation, margining, and variability analysis techniques that deepen your expertise in both SoC-level power and system-level behavior.

 Develop, implement, and maintain the DRP for critical IT systems and infrastructure.

 Assess potential risks, including natural disasters, cyberattacks, and technical failures, to ensure the organization is prepared to respond effectively.

 Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements and industry standards related to disaster recovery and business continuity.

 Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Business Continuity, or a related field.
 Minimum of 5 years of experience in disaster recovery, business continuity, or IT infrastructure management.
 Strong understanding of disaster recovery principles, including recovery time objectives (RTOs), recovery point objectives (RPOs), and backup strategies.
 Hands-on experience developing, implementing, and testing disaster recovery plans.
 Knowledge of IT infrastructure, including networks, servers, cloud environments, and data centers.
 Familiarity with relevant industry standards and frameworks, including ISO 22301 and NIST disaster recovery guidance.
 Strong organizational and project management skills, with attention to detail.
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams and external vendors.

 Experience with disaster recovery tools and platforms, including backup solutions, cloud recovery tools, and monitoring systems.

 Operations at Brex

 Own the credit policy, procedure, and exception monitoring cadence, and the regular reporting to second-line risk functions, with minimal oversight.

The Role 
 BeyondTrust is seeking a Senior Staff Software Development Engineer to set the technical direction for NHI Governance. NHI Governance is the Pathfinder Insights module that discovers, assesses, and remediates non-human identities — service principals, IAM users, access keys and secrets, workload identities, and AI agents — across Microsoft Entra ID, AWS, and on-premise environments. The system spans .NET 10 services over PostgreSQL; an inventory pipeline fed from governed Databricks lakehouse views; durable Temporal workflows (Python workers, a .NET gateway, protobuf contracts) that onboard, rotate, reduce access for, and decommission live customer credentials, with custody in BeyondTrust Password Safe and storage adapters for AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, and HashiCorp Vault; and Angular micro-frontends in the Insights console. It ships through GitOps to Amazon EKS in commercial and government environments.
 As one of the most senior engineers on the team, you will own the architecture across these pieces and the contracts that hold them together, lead the system from prototype to hardened production, and act as a force multiplier for a team that works in an AI-assisted, agent-native way.
 What You’ll Do 
 Own end-to-end architecture for NHI Governance across its services, the workflow layer it shares with the platform team, and the data lineage from the Insights lakehouse — and decide where each boundary lives.
 Design the source and vault plug-in seams (today Entra and AWS are bespoke), so a new identity source or vault becomes a repeatable, conformance-tested addition rather than a rewrite.
 Define and evolve the contracts other teams build on: service APIs and protobuf workflow schemas with breaking-change gates.
 Set the safety model for credential-lifecycle automation — rotation, decommissioning, access reduction, approvals, compensation, and points of no return — where a defect can revoke a customer's production credential.
 Define the least-privilege permission model customers grant us in Entra ID, AWS, and Password Safe, feature by feature. Own how it is verified live and explained in the product, and the setup assets (scripts, templates) that grant exactly that and no more.
 Lead the path from prototype to production: service-to-service authentication, tenant isolation, FIPS-compliant builds, and promotion through commercial and government environments.
 Design how our own services obtain identities and secrets across AWS accounts, regions, and environments — least privilege, workload identity, no long-lived keys.
 Partner with product, platform, data, and security leaders to align technical strategy with the roadmap; make the build/buy and architectural trade-off calls.
 Raise how the team builds: design reviews, testing against real dependencies and live test tenants, and the conventions and guardrails for AI-assisted development.
 Mentor staff and senior engineers and grow technical leadership on the team.
 What You’ll Bring 
 Deep expertise architecting and operating large-scale, multi-tenant, distributed cloud services, with a track record of owning architecture across multiple teams or an entire domain.
 Expert in C#/.NET, plus working proficiency in Python — our Temporal workers and every activity that touches a credential are Python. (Equivalent depth in another typed backend language is fine if you can lead a .NET codebase.)
 Production experience with durable or long-running workflow orchestration (e.g., Temporal, AWS Step Functions, Durable Functions) and event-driven systems (e.g., Kafka) — idempotency, retries, compensation, and workflow versioning.
 Hands-on experience building or operating systems that create, rotate, or revoke credentials — cloud access keys, service principals and app registrations, certificates, or vault-held secrets — and a sound instinct for blast radius.
 PAM or vault platform integration experience: managed accounts, rotation plugins, functional accounts. BeyondTrust Password Safe a plus.
 AWS at design level: you have designed how services obtain identity and secrets in production across multiple accounts and environments — least-privilege IAM, workload identity (e.g., IRSA or OIDC federation) instead of long-lived keys, Secrets Manager and KMS, and infrastructure as code (Terraform/Terragrunt).
 Azure at working level: Microsoft Entra ID app registrations and service principals, Microsoft Graph permissions and admin consent, managed identities, and Key Vault.
 Experience defining and versioning API and schema contracts (OpenAPI, protobuf) consumed by multiple teams.
 Production familiarity with Kubernetes (EKS preferred) and GitOps delivery.
 Excellent communication; able to influence technical direction across teams and with leadership.
 Comfortable working in an AI-assisted codebase and setting the standard for how AI-generated code is reviewed — especially changes that touch permissions.
 Nice To Have 
 Deep identity-security domain experience: IAM, NHI and secrets management, OAuth/OIDC, privileged access management.
 Delivery in regulated or government environments (FedRAMP, FIPS 140, AWS GovCloud).
 Additional identity models (GCP service accounts, GitHub Apps and tokens, Okta).
 Lakehouse / Databricks pipelines, including row-level security and governed data access; graph data modeling.
 Service mesh and mTLS.
 Daily hands-on practice with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code.
 Taking a module from 0 to 1 at enterprise scale.
 Who You Are 
 A technical authority who takes ownership of the hardest problems and delivers scalable, safe solutions.
 A force multiplier who elevates the engineers and teams around you.
 Someone who balances technical excellence with pragmatic decision-making, ensuring security without unnecessary complexity.

About Clutch: 
 Clutch is Canada’s largest online used car retailer, helping customers buy and sell cars from home. From browsing vehicles online to doorstep delivery and our 10-Day Money-Back Guarantee, we’re making the experience simpler from start to finish.
 Founded in 2017 and headquartered in Toronto, we’re growing quickly and looking for curious, driven people who want to help shape how Canadians buy, sell, and own cars. Learn more at clutch.ca .
 About the role: 
 Every car Clutch buys and sells starts with a pricing decision. For sellers, it’s the offer they accept or walk away from. For buyers, it’s one of the first things they compare. We’re hiring a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to help build the framework behind those decisions, from what we pay for a vehicle to what we list it for and how its price changes over time.
 You’ll build models, turn predictions into pricing decisions, and design experiments to measure their impact. You’ll own your work through production, including the pipelines, monitoring, and evaluation that keep models reliable. Because pricing outcomes can take weeks to emerge, you’ll also develop faster signals to help us understand what’s working.
 You’ll sit on Clutch’s pricing team and partner closely with acquisition, retail operations, finance, product, and engineering. Your work will be visible, measurable, and directly tied to margins, inventory performance, and the customer experience.
 What you’ll do: 
 Build the models behind vehicle valuation, expected sale proceeds, and time to sale, owning feature engineering, model development, calibration, and retraining.
 Turn model predictions into pricing decisions that account for business constraints, using optimization methods and thoughtful problem formulation.
 Own evaluation, building offline metrics that reflect business outcomes and using holdouts and historical replays to distinguish real improvements from random variation.
 Take your models into production and keep them reliable, owning training pipelines, serving, consistency between training and serving features, monitoring, and drift detection.
 Design and analyze experiments to understand how pricing changes affect vehicle sales and business performance.
 Work with analysts and operations teams to turn their market knowledge into useful model inputs and investigate quickly when predictions don’t reflect reality.
 Quantify the impact of pricing improvements and turn your findings into clear recommendations on where to invest next.
 What we’re looking for: 
 Must Haves 
 Production ML experience: 6+ years in a hands-on machine learning role, with a track record of models that improved business outcomes. You’ve owned models from training through deployment and ongoing operation, including pipelines, versioning, monitoring, and tools such as MLflow.
 Breadth across modeling approaches: Experience with deep learning for regression and classification, recommender systems, statistical modeling, experiment design, and linear and nonlinear constrained optimization. You have depth in several areas and can build working competence in the others.
 Strong engineering fundamentals: Strong Python and SQL, along with experience building services, writing tests, and working with CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, and orchestration.
 Statistical rigor: You can design and analyze A/B tests, choose methods appropriate to the underlying distributions, and reason about identification, confounding, variance, sample size, and power.
 Business judgment: You know how to connect model performance to business results and identify which problems are worth solving.
 Clear communication: You can explain technical findings and trade-offs to nontechnical partners, make actionable recommendations, and hold a thoughtful point of view when challenged.
 Nice to Have 
 Experience with pricing, revenue management, or marketplace dynamics.
 Working knowledge of TypeScript, which is used in much of the application consuming these models.
 Experience with causal inference and quasi-experimental methods when randomization isn’t available.
 Analytics engineering experience, including warehouse models, data contracts, and testing.
 Experience with physical inventory where individual units are unique, depreciate, and carry holding costs, particularly automotive, wholesale auctions, or vehicle valuation.
 What success looks like: 
 In the first 3 months: You understand the pricing framework, its weaknesses, and their business impact. You’ve identified an opportunity, developed a hypothesis, and run an experiment to test it.
 By 6 months: You own one or more parts of the framework. Your work has delivered measurable business value, and you can demonstrate what drove the improvement.
 By 12 months: You’ve identified and built a missing capability. Your findings are changing how Clutch makes pricing decisions.
 Why you’ll love it at Clutch: 
 Ownership of meaningful problems, with room to shape your approach and see it through.
 Competitive pay and the opportunity to share in Clutch’s growth through stock options.
 Time off to rest and recharge.
 Health and dental coverage to support you and your family.
 Employment Type: 
 New, Permanent Full-Time.
 Hybrid, with three days per week at our downtown Toronto office.
 Compensation & Benefits: 
 Annual Base Salary: $180,000+ CAD.
 Equity: Stock options.
 Coverage: Healthcare, dental, vision, prescription drugs, life insurance, and coverage for eligible dependents.
 Compensation considers relevant skills, performance, market benchmarks, role responsibilities, and working conditions.

No matter the location, we tailor our experience to ensure our employees are creative, productive, and happy.
 The Team 
 Apollo leads Block's work on the Customer World Model : a continuously evolving representation of each customer's goals, context, history, constraints, and likely future needs. The Customer World Model powers Proactive Intelligence across Block's ecosystem, including Square, Cash App, and Afterpay. Instead of customers searching through products for the feature they need, the system understands what matters to them, anticipates what comes next, and takes timely action that improves their outcomes. Both are top priorities for Block.
 The Role 
 We're hiring exceptional AI Researchers to take Customer World Model and Proactive Intelligence from promising research to reliable production systems. You'll set the technical direction, solve the hardest research and engineering problems, and own delivery all the way through production integration.  Deep expertise in modern machine learning, including representation learning, sequence or foundation models, and forecasting or decision-making under uncertainty.
